subject: Post-call: throughput split & streaming window assumptions for ZingerPilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Vargas <alex.vargas@zinger.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: throughput split & streaming window assumptions for ZingerPilot

Alex — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap focused on the perf requirements so we have a shared baseline for sizing. I pulled together the numbers you mentioned and noted a few clarifying questions; please correct anything I misunderstood.

Key points from our call:
- Primary flow is the consumer chat endpoint (long-running streaming responses) and a shorter synchronous prompt endpoint used by admin tools.
- Typical steady-state: ~85 QPS across the chat endpoint, average user message ~220 tokens.
- Peak windows: up to ~1,700 QPS for 30–45s spikes driven by marketing campaign activity; sustained peak can hit ~400 QPS for 10–15 minutes during batch jobs.
- Streaming semantics: single connection per user; we expect per-token latency SLO of 150ms P95 for the streaming path (end-to-end from request to first token and subsequent token cadence at ~35–40ms per token).
- Concurrency: roughly 18–22 concurrent streams per GPU expected for your target model family (you cited an LLM variant similar size to Llama-2-13B).

Clarifications I need to finalize our sizing recommendation:
1) Tokenization: do you observe average generated token count per response in production (not just user prompt length)? You mentioned 340 tokens on first call — is that median or 95th?
2) Traffic shape: can you confirm whether campaign spikes have a gradual ramp (minutes) or are bursty (seconds)? This affects autoscaler warmup.
3) Retries/backoff: any client-side retry patterns (e.g., 2-second retry on failures) that could amplify peak QPS?

Attached: a quick CSV I exported from your onboarding telemetry and a sketch of the streaming window assumptions. I’ll iterate a draft capacity plan once I get your clarifications — aiming to present a recommendation (dedicated pool vs. hosted multi-tenant with burst) by next Wednesday.

Next steps I propose:
- Alex to confirm items 1–3 above (reply inline).
- Redwood (Marissa + Priyom) to run a narrowbench simulation against your sample traffic (we’ll need an API key scoped to a dev model).
- Follow-up call to review sizing matrix and cost tradeoffs: propose Tue 2026-12-02 10:00 PT.

Thanks — Karthik

--

Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput split & streaming window assumptions for ZingerPilot

Thanks Karthik — good summary. Quick replies inline below and a couple of extra data points.

> 1) Tokenization: do you observe average generated token count per response in production (not just user prompt length)? You mentioned 340 tokens on first call — is that median or 95th?

Median generated tokens is ~310; 95th is ~920 (largely due to some long-form assistant responses for troubleshooting flows). The 340 I quoted was an average from a week sample — agree median is better to use for steady-state.

> 2) Traffic shape: can you confirm whether campaign spikes have a gradual ramp (minutes) or are bursty (seconds)?

Campaigns are mostly bursty at the start (seconds-level fan-out) for the first ~20–40s then tail off over 3–4 minutes. The 1,700 QPS micro-spike is typically <60s.

> 3) Retries/backoff: any client-side retry patterns 

We have simplistic client retry: 2 attempts with exponential backoff starting at 500ms; however the mobile SDK sometimes triggers immediate reconnects on network flaps which can create short amplification. We can instrument a guard if this looks problematic.

Extra: attaching the small CSV you requested from our ops export (zinger_throughput_snapshot.csv). Also sent the streaming window diagram.

I can confirm we can provide a dev key with rate-limits suited for a narrowbench run — will coordinate with SRE (cc’d). Tue 2026-12-02 10:00 PT works for me.

— Alex
Alex Vargas

Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput split & streaming window assumptions for ZingerPilot

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Alex — this is very helpful. A couple of follow-up notes based on the numbers: 

- Sizing implication: using median generated tokens (310) and steady-state 85 QPS we estimate sustained token throughput ~26.4k tokens/s; during the 1,700 QPS micro-spike using median tokens that becomes ~527k tokens/s if all requests are short responses. That delta is what pushes us to recommend a mixed approach: a small dedicated pool sized for steady-state + intelligent burst routing (hosted burst or transient reserved capacity) for the micro-spikes.
- Streaming latency: our default streaming configuration can meet 150ms P95 first-token with adequate prefix caching and per-request KV allocation, but the 35–40ms cadence per token will need tuning at the model kernel level; we’ll include a quantization/perf profile in the narrowbench.
- Autoscaler warmup: because spikes are seconds-level, we’ll recommend a pre-warmed burst lane and connection throttling at the client to prevent retry amplification.

Action items: 
- Marissa: run narrowbench against the dev key Alex will provide and attach perf profile by EOD 2026-12-03.
- Priyom: prepare a draft capacity matrix (dedicated baseline + burst lanes) and cost delta for hosted burst vs. reserved burst by 2026-12-04.
- Alex: send the dev API key and confirm any IP allowlists/time windows you want for the test.

I’ll pull these into a one-page recommendation and share before our Tue sync. If anything here looks off, flag in reply.

Thanks — Karthik
